author: NorthEast News Desk
body: BRICS negotiators reached agreement on a joint declaration Saturday as leaders began summit talks in New Delhi, according to four sources familiar with the discussions. The reported deal is a significant test of the expanded group’s ability to maintain consensus while members Iran and the United Arab Emirates remain divided over the Gulf conflict.

The sources said the draft was unlikely to name any country but would condemn unilateral aggression. Leaders were expected to consider the document later Saturday. India’s foreign ministry did not immediately comment on the reported agreement. Host Prime Minister Narendra Modi opened the summit by urging members to turn their shared positions into concrete results and renewed his call for reform of the United Nations Security Council.

A BRICS foreign ministers’ meeting in May ended without a joint statement because members could not bridge their differences. The declaration therefore represents a diplomatic advance even before final approval. BRICS is also seeking greater influence over international financial and trade institutions. Details may change as leaders debate and approve the final text.
dek: Negotiators agreed on language that sources said would condemn unilateral aggression without naming a country, with leaders expected to consider it Saturday.
headline: BRICS reaches joint-declaration deal despite Middle East divisions
